cases.excerpt: Data from 11 cohort studies in the BLadder cancer Epidemiology and Nutritional Determinants (BLEND) study, provided sufficient information on fat intake for a total of 2731 BC cases and 544 452 noncases, which yielded 5 400 168 person-years of follow-up.

effect_size.excerpt: Among women, an inverse association was observed between mono-unsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs) and BC risk (HR comparing the highest with the lowest tertile: 0.73, 95% CI: 0.58-0.93, P-trend = .01).

studies.Reference: Fatty Acid Intake and Bladder Cancer Risk: A Multicenter Case-Control Study in Iran.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Conversely, OR for high intake of palmitoleic acid, alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), and docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) was elevated.
extraction_supporting_text.design: Fatty Acid Intake and Bladder Cancer Risk: A Multicenter Case-Control Study in Iran.

extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire.
extraction_supporting_text.gender: Sex-specific effects were found stearic acid was protective in men, while PUFAs were protective in women.
